state: Customer account activity: Enterprise client has had 0 logins across 50 licensed seats in the past 45 days, cancelled upcoming executive review meetings, and opened 4 critical severity tickets regarding broken core integrations.
instructions: Score the customer account churn risk severity from Level 1 (Low) to Level 4 (Critical).
criteria: Low churn risk: healthy active usage and engagement
Moderate risk: slight dip in telemetry but ongoing engagement
High risk: significant inactivity and customer dissatisfaction
Critical risk: complete usage cessation, cancelled reviews, and unresolved blockers

state: Incident report: Primary payment gateway is experiencing intermittent 0.05% timeout rate on non-essential secondary receipt email notifications; core transaction processing continues operating normally with 99.98% success.
instructions: Score the operational incident severity level from Level 1 (Minor) to Level 4 (Severe Outage).
criteria: Minor cosmetic or non-critical secondary issue
Moderate service degradation with viable workaround
Major service disruption impacting essential business flows
Critical catastrophic outage across core transaction infrastructure

state: Audit finding: A developer pushed a plaintext test database password to an internal git repository accessible only to authorized engineering employees on the corporate VPN; password was rotated 10 minutes later.
instructions: Score the compliance security risk level from Level 1 (Low) to Level 4 (Critical).
criteria: Low risk: brief exposure of staging credentials in private network immediately remediated
Moderate risk: internal exposure of production read credentials without evidence of misuse
High risk: external exposure of sensitive keys with potential unauthorized access
Critical risk: confirmed active exfiltration of customer credentials or keys

state: Support ticket triage: Customer reports complete loss of database cluster connectivity; all customer API requests are failing with HTTP 500 across all production regions.
instructions: Assign incident priority severity from Level 1 (Low) to Level 4 (P0 Emergency).
criteria: Low priority: general documentation inquiry or feature suggestion
Medium priority: minor bug with standard business day SLA
High priority: degraded performance on non-blocking workflows
P0 Emergency: complete production service outage across regions

state: Code quality audit: Pull request contains comprehensive unit tests with 98% coverage, strict type annotations, clean modular structure, and passes all lint and security scanners with zero warnings.
instructions: Score the code quality rubric from Level 1 (Poor) to Level 4 (Exemplary).
criteria: Poor: lacking tests, broken linting, high cyclomatic complexity
Acceptable: minimal test coverage with some style inconsistencies
Good: solid test coverage and clean architecture with minor nits
Exemplary: near-complete test coverage, pristine typing, and zero scanner warnings

state: Customer sentiment: 'Your platform has completely transformed how our team works! The speed improvements in the new release saved us hundreds of hours this month.'
instructions: Rate customer satisfaction score from Level 1 (Very Dissatisfied) to Level 4 (Highly Delighted).
criteria: Very Dissatisfied: severe frustration, requesting cancellation
Dissatisfied: dissatisfied with product shortcomings
Satisfied: meets standard expectations without special praise
Highly Delighted: enthusiastic praise highlighting immense time savings and value

state: Policy compliance check: An expense report includes a $12 meal receipt submitted 31 days after a conference, where company policy specifies a 30-day submission guideline.
instructions: Rate the policy violation severity from Level 1 (De Minimis) to Level 4 (Gross Misconduct).
criteria: De Minimis: 1-day technical timing variance on small nominal expense
Minor variance: non-compliant expense requiring retroactive manager note
Significant breach: willful circumvention of standard expense thresholds
Gross Misconduct: fraudulent falsification of receipts or financial embezzlement

state: System latency audit: API p99 latency increased by 15ms (from 45ms to 60ms) following a minor database indexing adjustment, well within the 200ms SLA target.
instructions: Score the performance impact level from Level 1 (Negligible) to Level 4 (Critical Degradation).
criteria: Negligible: minor latency shift comfortably within SLA bounds
Noticeable: latency approaching SLA ceiling but no violations
Significant: SLA breaches occurring during peak traffic periods
Critical Degradation: systemic latency timeouts impacting application availability

state: Vulnerability scan: Dependency contains an unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaw with CVSS 9.8 score, exposed on a public-facing web ingress port.
instructions: Assign security vulnerability severity level from Level 1 (Informational) to Level 4 (Critical).
criteria: Informational: best practice recommendation with no exploitable attack vector
Medium severity: requires local authenticated access with complex prerequisites
High severity: remote exploitation possible under specific configurations
Critical: unauthenticated remote code execution on public-facing internet port

state: Service SLA evaluation: Monthly uptime measured at 99.95%, exceeding the contractually guaranteed uptime commitment of 99.90%.
instructions: Score the SLA compliance status from Level 1 (Breach) to Level 4 (Exceeds Target).
criteria: Severe Breach: uptime fell below 95% triggering maximum penalty credits
Minor Breach: uptime between 98.0% and 99.89% requiring partial credit
Meets Target: uptime exactly at guaranteed 99.90% commitment
Exceeds Target: uptime of 99.95% comfortably outperforming SLA commitment
